newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends higher with crude, Skikda reopens.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends higher with crude, Skikda reopens.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady to higher on Wednesday, piggybacking recent gains in crude and gasoline after Algeria's Skikda port reopened on Wednesday for oil tankers.
"It's not altered the perception in the market," said one source, of the port reopening. "It's bullish from a trader's perspective...The end-users are not interested because of the high prices."
He said supplies of certain grade and size were relatively scarce in NWE, supporting prices even though the cargo prices were up only on a notional basis.

A bid for 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes of pipeline spec material for delivery by December 15 was seen earlier at $230 and the buyer was apparently willing to pay up to $231 by the end of the day, sources said.
Dec swaps ended $1 higher at $230/$231 with Jan holding at a $9.50 backwardation, at $220.50/$221.50.
With the market's backwardation, NWE cargoes were valued about $2 above Dec swaps at $232/$234 cif and barges $3 below cargoes at $229/$231 fob ARA.
